concept.name: opposed-flight glance / split landing debt
concept.force_problem: two independently airborne bodies collide glancingly; transient body-body impulse bends both free-flight velocity vectors without granting support or custody; they separate immediately and pay unequal staggered landing debts
concept.novelty_vs_prior: external second-body impulse is the cause; unlike payload acquisition there is no custody/shared-mass descent, unlike hook/catch there is no sustained anchor, unlike midair recoil pulse the vector bend is not self-task-generated, and unlike moving-support undercatch no support exists until separate ground catches
concept.contact_law: contact is an authored transient constraint/impulse, never support; the last clear state remains visibly separated and the first collision geometry is the authored contact key; contact ends before either ground acquisition
concept.support_law: both NONE through collision; A earns right-foot ground first; B remains free; B later earns left-foot ground; both pay separate compression and secondary-lag recovery

keys.pose_B: B wide stance, far shoulder still slightly high
